title: CP/M-65, pkIntvMCP and Level 9 discovery review
summary: Review an old Level 9 source and four rotated GitHub code-search routes; add CP/M-65 and pkIntvMCP, and refresh the reconstructed Level 9 toolchain.
notes: The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved source or target CPU areas before candidate selection. Exact GitHub code-search queries were `Intellivision disassembly`, `Oric Atmos homebrew`, `TRS-80 Color Computer disassembly`, and `Sharp MZ source reconstruction`. Primary repository evidence was reviewed for two new candidates. The TRS-80/CoCo route resolved to the already tracked Computer Archeology project; the Sharp MZ route returned no relevant retro-development candidate. No upstream software, ROM, image, test suite, compiler or emulator was executed. Build and runtime flags reflect bounded primary-source claims only.

sources.reason: Primary repository for the TypeScript CP-1600 emulator, disassembler and MCP debugging server.
Primary repository for CP/M-65, a native CP/M port and development environment for 6502-family retro systems.

Fresh-search slice. Exact query `Intellivision disassembly` surfaced peterkaminski/pkintvmcp, whose pinned README, MCP server, package manifest and current commit attribution were reviewed and promoted. Other returned roots were already tracked, generic emulators, curated indexes or unrelated keyword co-occurrences.

Fresh-search slice. Exact query `Oric Atmos homebrew` surfaced davidgiven/cpm65. Its pinned README and repository implementation tree were reviewed; the Oric port is one of many coherent CP/M-65 targets, so one repository-root project was promoted rather than a platform-fragment record.

Fresh-search slice. Exact query `TRS-80 Color Computer disassembly` returned the already tracked Computer Archeology collection as its material candidate. Other results were indexes, broad emulators, unrelated repositories or documentation-only matches; no new candidate was promoted.

Fresh-search slice. Exact query `Sharp MZ source reconstruction` produced only modern machine-learning and incidental text matches in the reviewed result page; no Sharp MZ retro-development candidate URL was identified.

source_updates.reason: Rechecked the current repository root and l9dev at commit 02aaab0a9326292b01b213c727528e39b0d7e2a5. The reconstructed C toolchain now includes ST and PC machine-code interpreters, debug/autorun modes, text-only HUGE support, game selection and expanded regression fixtures; missing v1-v2 messaging/input and graphics remain explicit limitations. The root game/sys/floppy archive graph is now substantially reviewed, while its broad ecosystem tracking task remains open.

task_updates.notes_append: Reviewed the current Level9-Public root and l9dev expansion at 02aaab0a9326292b01b213c727528e39b0d7e2a5. The existing l9dev project now covers the added ST/PC interpreter and regression scope; no separate title was split from the coherent toolchain. Other sources named by this broad task remain open.

project.title: pkIntvMCP
project.display_title: pkIntvMCP — AI-assisted CP-1600 emulator and debugger

runtime_profiles.name: Node.js MCP server and CLI
runtime_profiles.notes: The root package manifest states the host runtime versions. No host CPU or RAM minimum is documented or inferred.

project.status: Alpha CP-1600 emulator and MCP debugger; full Intellivision system integration and external jzIntv validation remain incomplete

evidence: Latest reviewed commit explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and carries a Claude Sonnet 4.5 co-author trailer: f518a181e9c6abe51661471de495a2009290de13

identity.narrative: The repository identifies pkIntvMCP as Peter Kaminski's CP-1600/Intellivision emulator and debugging tool, with a TypeScript workspace containing core, CLI and MCP-server packages.

classification.narrative: This is modern retro-development tooling: it emulates and disassembles CP-1600 instructions, exposes execution and inspection through MCP, and is designed for debugging or reverse-engineering Intellivision ROMs. It is not a game reconstruction or full gameplay emulator.

source_cpu.narrative: The reviewed implementation and documentation explicitly target CP-1600/Intellivision machine code; the tracker uses the established General Instrument CP1610 catalogue label for that source architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The output is host-side TypeScript tooling rather than a generated retro-machine binary. No fixed host instruction set is assigned from Node.js or the development language.

build.narrative: The workspace provides build and test scripts, a runnable CLI and an implemented stdio MCP server. The README reports 348 passing tests and a complete 79-instruction CPU core, while also marking the project alpha and external jzIntv validation incomplete.
build.limitations: The tracker did not install dependencies, build, run tests, execute ROMs or compare behavior with jzIntv. The README's earlier planning prose is partly stale relative to the implemented MCP server.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The root package manifest explicitly requires Node.js 18 or newer and npm 9 or newer for the host tools. No CPU, RAM or operating-system minimum is stated.

ai.narrative: The latest reviewed commit explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and includes a Claude Sonnet 4.5 co-author trailer. Claude is also the intended conversational debugging client, but that integration alone is kept separate from the contribution evidence.

relationships.narrative: The README explicitly positions jzIntv as the reference emulator and says pkIntvMCP is a debugging/analysis companion rather than a replacement. External validation against jzIntv is still pending.

project.title: CP/M-65
project.display_title: CP/M-65 — native CP/M port for 6502-family systems

runtime_profiles.name: Atari 400/800 XL/XE disk build
runtime_profiles.notes: The standard disk and hard-disk builds run with at least 16 KiB; the XL/XE-specific xlhd build requires at least 64 KiB.

runtime_profiles.name: Oric 1 / Oric Atmos Microdisc build
runtime_profiles.notes: Oric 1 requires the full 64 KiB upgrade including overlay RAM; only the Microdisc interface currently works reliably.

runtime_profiles.name: Fully expanded VIC-20 build
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires a fully expanded VIC-20 with all memory banks populated for the full 35 KiB configuration; several drive/loader image variants have different peripheral requirements.

runtime_profiles.name: Ohio Scientific build
runtime_profiles.notes: README states support for Ohio Scientific systems with at least 16 KiB and a floppy drive.

runtime_profiles.name: Apple IIe build
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires an 80-column card but explicitly does not require auxiliary memory; two slot-6 drives are supported.

project.status: Native 6502-family CP/M port with binary releases, cross/native development tools and broad hardware support

identity.narrative: David Given's repository identifies CP/M-65 as a native port of Digital Research's CP/M to the 6502, with a coherent operating system, applications, libraries, build system, disk images and tests.

classification.narrative: This is a native reimplementation/port of the CP/M operating environment for 6502-family machines, with relocatable application binaries and both cross-hosted and native development tools. It is not labelled binary-derived reverse engineering.

source_cpu.narrative: The README contrasts CP/M-65 with original 8080 CP/M programs and explicitly says it does not run 8080 binaries; Intel 8080 is recorded as the source architecture of the operating-system subject, not as an emulated CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The repository documents native 6502 and 65C02 machines and a Super Nintendo build using 65816 code; these are explicit output architectures, not inferred from platform names alone.

build.narrative: README supplies binary releases and an llvm-mos-based Makefile workflow that builds bootable images for supported targets. It also documents automated MAME tests for a subset of platforms and native/cross development tools.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build the aggregate dependency graph, download ROMs, run MAME, write media or boot any image. Peripheral and emulator limitations differ by platform.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed README provides explicit memory or hardware requirements for Atari, Oric, fully expanded VIC-20, Ohio Scientific and Apple IIe variants. Only those stated requirements are captured; other platform model names are not converted into guessed CPU or RAM minima.

ai.narrative: The inspected primary README, root tree and pinned head commit contain no explicit development-AI contribution disclosure. This bounded absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The project is explicitly related to Digital Research CP/M but produces native relocatable 6502-family applications rather than emulating or translating existing 8080 binaries. Its many machine ports are one coherent repository-level operating-system project.

project.status: Reconstructed Linux toolchain with ST/PC interpreters, HUGE text-only support and regression fixtures; graphics and v1-v2 support remain incomplete

runtime_profiles.name: Linux l9dev tools and interpreters
runtime_profiles.notes: The README provides make/install instructions and Ubuntu 24.04 binaries. No host CPU or RAM minimum is stated or inferred.

identity.narrative: The l9dev directory remains one coherent reconstruction of Level 9's development tools, recoded in C from Atari ST 68000 assembler. The current source now includes compiler, finisher, squasher, menu and interpreter programs.

classification.narrative: The project is both a source reconstruction of historical Level 9 authoring tools and an active Linux compiler/interpreter environment useful for preserved game sources. New interpreters expand the same toolchain rather than constituting a separate project.

source_cpu.narrative: The primary README explicitly says the C tools were recoded from Atari ST 68000 assembler, establishing m68000 as the historical source architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The reconstructed tools are host C programs for Linux; no fixed Linux host CPU is documented. Their optional generation or interpretation of ST/PC machine code is a tool capability, not a minimum host CPU.

build.narrative: The current Makefile builds l9comp, l9finish, l9int, l9menu and l9squash with GCC, while scripts drive game generation and table assembly. The README documents ST/PC interpreter modes, text-only HUGE support and compile/run regression suites.
build.limitations: No local compilation or regression run was performed. The README explicitly leaves graphics, v1-v2 messaging/input and broader packaging incomplete, and lists missing or corrupted historical inputs.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README provides Ubuntu 24.04 executables and a generic Linux make/install route. No minimum host processor or RAM is stated, so none is inferred.

ai.narrative: The inspected l9dev README, Makefile and current head commit provide no explicit development-AI contribution disclosure. This does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The toolchain is derived from Level 9's Atari ST 68000 authoring programs, incorporates observed v1.5 behavior, and credits the GS/DK interpreter for verification. Preserved game sources and regression fixtures are inputs/tests, not separate l9dev implementations.

decisions.title: pkIntvMCP — AI-assisted CP-1600 emulator and debugger
decisions.reason: Implemented TypeScript CP-1600 core, disassembler, execution controls and MCP inspection server form a substantive Intellivision debugging and binary-analysis environment. Full-system emulation and external jzIntv validation remain incomplete.

decisions.title: CP/M-65 — native CP/M port for 6502-family systems
decisions.reason: Coherent native CP/M reimplementation targets many 6502, 65C02 and 65816 machines, provides relocatable applications and development tools, and documents build, release, test and hardware-specific runtime requirements. It does not emulate 8080 binaries.
